As per the title, I'm looking for some recommendations here.

My kiddos have recently graduated from paved trails and we're moving on to bigger and rockier things. My backpack I've been using just doesn't seem to have enough pockets. As of now we're only going into the trail about 2-3 miles (4-6 mi round trip), but it's 26 miles long so I expect that distance to grow. I need something mainly to hold water and snacks (for 1 adult 3 kids), bug stuff, a waterproof/resistant portion for electronics and I'm guessing I should start looking into a first aid kit. Honestly, I have no idea what I'm doing. Any recommendations or advice for packs would be much appreciated. Any advice on growing into this hobby would be great too.

I gather that you're mainly looking at day hikes so far. The best advice anyone can give you on a pack, is to go to your local EMS/REI/whatever outdoors stores in your area and try packs on. Look for ones that have enough space for the things you mentioned, and choose from there. The biggest factor in choosing a pack is the comfort, and that's something only you can answer.
Thanks for your reply, trying them on makes a lot of sense. Are there any brands I should avoid or features I'll wish I looked for once I advance beyond the beginner stage?

When it comes to day packs, there's no wrong answer. Personally, I carry a ~20ish liter pack that came equipped with a bladder. It's made by Camelback, and I haven't been disappointed with it at all for the last 8 years. It's all about budget for beginners, and there's nothing wrong with getting a $30 bag that's going to work well for the next year or two. As far as features, you already know what you need space for currently. If you don't see that changing in the next couple of years, get a cheaper bag, and make notes of what doesn't work for you over time.

Edit: I read your post over again, and I thought you might care for a few tips.

  • DON'T cheap out on a first aid kit. It's the single most important thing in your pack, and you may never have to use it. It is always best to over-protect in this case.

  • A GPS device is handy, but always bring a map and compass (and know how to use them!) as a backup.

  • Always bring a few extra snacks/a little extra water. You never know when you might want that third Cliff bar.

  • Change of socks. ALWAYS.

  • Did I mention the first aid kit?

  • A whistle is good to have if you're not familiar with the area and are afraid of getting lost.

  • Hat/Sunglasses/SPF/DEET - because you'll thank yourself later.
I never would've thought about socks until it was too late. I'm heading down to REI this weekend to look around and try some things on. Thanks for the tips, they'll definitely not go to waste!

Yeah, I learned that lesson the hard way several times over. The folks over at REI should be able to point you in the right direction as far as packs go, but you should probably have some idea of features you want before going in; things like water bladder, headphone slot, waterproof, etc.

MNUFC look towards St Paul for new MLS Stadium

The club just posted this link via their Facebook.

It looks like they are now considering St Paul as a potential site for the stadium after talks have soured with Minneapolis officials over the past few months.

All in all, I'm happy to see the investment group look at other options, as it appears that the council is unwilling to event come to the table to talk. For those wondering what the history of this was, after winning the bid for MLS expansion, MNUFC looked to finance a stadium in downtown Minneapolis. However, after the Wilfs and Vikings ownership did not get the MLS bid to make the new MLS team their bitch they started to get passive aggressive towards Minnesota United (in true Minnesota fashion). I'll try to be less sour about how I feel about this council that shelled out a billion dollars of tax money on a Vikings Stadium, more money at the St Paul Saints (minor league Baseball) yet won't come to the negotiating table for a professional soccer team that is entirely privately funded but seeks tax incentives. Meanwhile the Target Center just got 30 million more dollars to renovate the home of the Timberwolves last March.

I can respect that people do not want to see more public funds go into another stadium, but MNUFC has brought a completely privately funded proposal that will put some money into redeveloping the farmer's market area. Property tax was valued at 3M a year and MNUFC was seeking to lock in the tax rate (i.e. not see this go up) for 30 years but this can be negotiated down.

Ultimately I don't think that Minneapolis is the only option and I'm happy to have more reasons to explore St Paul on a weekend.

Especially with the Green line up and running now, St. Paul is a perfectly viable option. I'd prefer Minneapolis, but mostly I just want this MLS team to happen, regardless of where the stadium ends up.
